title: Apatra Biosensor field intake scratch
content:
Summary:

Short capture from 2026-02-26 call with Apatra (wearable biosensor vendor). They're doing an in-clinic field pilot (50 devices/day) and want an on-prem/private Redwood deployment in a hospital network (air-gapped-ish). Primary use: real-time signal-cleaning + short clinical note summarization from sensor telemetry and nurse annotations.

Attendees:
- Dr. Maya Reddy (Apatra clinical lead)
- Linh Tran (Apatra infra)
- Marco Sosa (Apatra product)
- Avery Chen (Redwood SE)
- Diego Morales (Redwood infra)

Context / mission:
- Apatra needs low-latency per-reading feedback (~200ms P95) for a short natural-language output (30-80 tokens) to present to nurse apps.
- Data policy: PHI stays inside hospital. They will host on-prem VMs in a private cluster with a dedicated NIC to Redwood Private control plane (VPN + KMS).
- Pilot scale: 50 devices concurrently, each sending 1 inference every ~10s during active monitoring windows. Peak concurrency estimate ~75 concurrent requests.

Primary success criteria (customer):
- P95 latency <= 220ms for typical 60-token outputs in steady-state
- 99.9% availability during shift hours (pilot SLA expectation)
- Local-only data (no outgoing telemetry) and HSM-backed keys for model encryption

Notes from conversation (raw / scratch):
- They currently run a tiny signal-cleaner on-device; Redwood model is called for de-noising and converting event windows to a short narrative and triage code.
- Want to avoid cold-starts — expect bursts when clinicians open queues. Concern about first-token latency after idle.
- Hospital ops team worried about GPU isolation and noisy-neighbor risk on shared node images.

Technical constraints / gotchas pointed out:
- Network egress is tightly restricted. Control-plane callbacks are allowed through an approved proxy, but anything failing to that proxy gets blocked by hospital NOC. Need explicit proxy IPs and certificate pinning notes.
- Kubernetes version is managed with strict security baseline (no hostPath mounts, restricted runtime), so our Private deployment scripts need adjustment to use CSI + sidecar for KV cache persisting.
- They prefer deterministic model inference—quantization must not introduce hallucination risk. Clinical accuracy guardrails required.
- Existing on-device batching is minimal; they expect Redwood to handle concurrency and batching on the server side.

Initial technical recommendations (SE quick-start):
- Model: start with an open 7B/13B foundation family (we suggested using a verified 7B fp16 model for earliest pilot to reduce cost and hit latency targets). If accuracy drops, move to 13B quantized (q4f16) after evals.
- Runtime settings: target per-request max tokens 80, prompt prefix short. Use continuous KV cache and per-session routing to keep warm runtimes. Suggest warm-up cron to keep at least N=4 workers hot during shift hours to avoid cold-start.
- Batching: enable small-window batching (max batch 16, latency cap 80ms) to maximize GPU throughput without breaking P95 SLO.
- Caching: prefix/KV caching for repetitive nurse-note patterns. Persist KV cache on fast NVMe via CSI.
- Isolation: Dedicated GPU pool (Redwood Dedicated style) inside their VPC equivalent. Prefer 1 GPU per 12 concurrent 13B streams as a starting heuristic; pilot likely fine with 1 x A5000 equivalent for 7B family.
- Monitoring: stream token-level latency metrics to their Splunk/ELK via allowed proxy; also configure quality regression hook to fire if token overlap/score drops below threshold on stored eval set.

Rough capacity math (back-of-envelope):
- Target workload: 75 concurrent requests, avg response length 60 tokens, model throughput estimate: 200 tokens/s for 7B on our optimized runtime (per-GPU steady).
- Token load: 75 * 60 tokens = 4500 tokens per second -> ~22.5k tokens per 5s window. At 200 tps per GPU, need ~23 GPUs to sustain purely serial workload. BUT continuous batching and short-avg-latency with q4 quantization improve this; realistic pilot with batching and optimized kernels could run on 2-3 mid-sized GPUs for 7B family. This is rough; must validate with perf tests.

Risk notes / unknowns:
- Clinical accuracy: must run a small eval suite with their annotated examples (they agreed to share 200 labeled windows). Run Redwood Optimize quality check and generate regression alerts.
- Quantization risk: some post-quantization regressions observed for numeric lab-value extraction in our older Q4 variants. Plan: do targeted unit tests on numeric extraction if they need precise lab formatting.
- Cold start: hospital network policy may tear down idle containers quicker than cloud default -> need keepalive/cron.

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Apatra: share 200 labeled telemetry->note pairs + sample device telemetry stream (Lin h) — due 2026-03-05.
- Redwood SE (Avery): run quick on-prem perf run in staging with candidate 7B fp16 model using their sample stream; capture P50/P95 under simulated concurrency (75). ETA 2026-03-10.
- Redwood Infra (Diego): prepare a Private deployment manifest variant that uses CSI driver + no hostPath, provide proxy-egress IP list and connection checklist. ETA 2026-03-04.
- Redwood Research (Priya): prepare a quick quantization risk note listing known regressions for numeric patterns and suggested mitigations. ETA 2026-03-07.
- Joint: schedule field-run dry day with hospital NOC to validate proxy & firewall rules. Target date: week of 2026-03-15.

Slack / comms shorthand:
- Created channel: #apatra-pilot (requesting NOC + security inclusion).
- Jira: create ENG-APATRA-1 (private-deploy manifest), ENG-APATRA-2 (perf run), ENG-APATRA-3 (eval set onboarding).

Open questions (for next call):
- How aggressive is their idle scaling policy? Need exact kubelet eviction config and container runtime timeout.
- Do they require model hermeticity (no model files stored on local disk) or is ephemeral disk + encrypted volume acceptable?
- Which HSM/KMS vendor (they mentioned "internal KMS" — need vendor + API).
- Any legal requirement for model provenance logging (we should log model version + sha per response).

Notes to self / informal TODOs:
- Walk through Private documentation with Linh once proxy details provided.
- Add small eval harness to Redwood Optimize to track 200 annotated examples; wire regression alerts to #apatra-pilot.
- Draft an ops-runbook snippet for hospital NOC (certificate pinning, ip ranges, permitted endpoints).

End of raw scratch. Will refine into a tidy one-pager once sample data landed.
